function.mechanism: Azo chromophore imparts red color by absorbing visible light.

adi.basis: EFSA re-evaluation ADI, carried into refined exposure assessment context

efsa.key_finding: EFSA refined exposure (2015) reported no ADI exceedance in refined scenarios, while earlier conservative scenarios could exceed ADI in children.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR Part 74 (food color listings) and 21 CFR 70.5

adi.basis: JECFA ADI expressed as 0-4 mg/kg bw

concerns.summary: A 2025 in vitro lymphocyte study reported genotoxic effects mainly at high concentrations for carmoisine and ponceau 4R.
Artificial-color mixture trial in children reported increased hyperactivity; effect was mixture-based, not azorubine-only.
Recent zebrafish and Drosophila studies report developmental/oxidative stress effects, including stronger signals in co-exposure conditions.

no_concern_confirmed: IARC classification dataset lists Carmoisine in Group 3.
EFSA refined exposure assessment (2015) did not exceed ADI in refined scenarios.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported potential exceedance in older conservative high-percentile scenarios, but not in refined 2015 scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: E122 is ADI-regulated and still authorized by EFSA/JECFA, but child-focused exposure caveats and accumulating mechanistic toxicity signals argue against a limited/risk-free tier.
